To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 137Cs induces gene expression changes in the blood that can be detected by microarray, 2) the gene expression pattern changes over time, 3) many of the genes and pathways affected have known roles in response to radiation exposure, and 4) the pattern of response to internal radiation is distinct from that seen after external exposure.

1) many radiation-responsive genes are expressed after a single injection of 137CsCl, but the expression pattern is extremely complex; 2) the expression of many Tp53 target genes is altered by 137CsCl; and 3) there are many differences in expression of radiation-responsive genes between internal and external radiation.

the gene expression response to internally administered 137Csis complex, with a large fraction of genes being up-regulated early after exposure, followed by a large fraction of down-regulated genes at later times, and many of the early genes are Tp53-regulation genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biomarkers for the early detection of internal radiation exposure.

the identification of genes and gene expression patterns that may serve as biomarkers for exposure to internally administered 137C, and that may provide insight into the biological mechanisms involved in this type of radiation exposure.
the molecular mechanisms of radiation-induced damage and repair, and with the development of methods to monitor and predict health consequences of radiation exposure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pattern of gene expression after a single dose of 137Cs is extremely complex and difficult to characterize in terms of a single gene expression signature.
137Cs is an extremely complex internal radiation source, and the resulting gene expression changes are equally complex.

the gene expression response to 137CsCl in the mouse is complex, with a pattern of gene expression that is not readily predictable, but which is consistent with a response to a chronic low dose rate exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
137CsCl exposure induces a complex, dynamic gene expression response in mice, and that the pattern of response is different from the response to acute external gamma-ray irradiation.
the gene expression response after a single dose of internal 137Cs is very complex and is not the same as that seen after an acute external exposure to gamma radiation.
the internal exposure to 137Cs results in an acute response, but also in a delayed, sustained response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
137CsCl administration is a useful tool for studying gene expression changes in the context of a long-lasting internal radiation exposure, but the pattern of gene expression is very complex.
137Cs is a powerful tool for studying the molecular response of the whole body to internal exposure.

137CsCl exposure induces a very complex pattern of gene expression changes that may be useful as biomarkers of exposure, but that these changes do not appear to be easily predictable from external exposure studies.
